{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study quantitatively compares the predictive accuracy of an in vitro ion channel assay (hERG) with a multi-ion channel assay (MICE) for predicting human torsade de pointes (TdP) outcomes, reporting sensitivity, specificity, and AUC values. It directly assesses the concordance between animal model (in vitro ion channel assays derived from animal models) and human clinical results.",
  "arm": "safety-pharmacology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study evaluates the predictive accuracy of in vitro ion channel assays (hERG, Cav1.2, Nav1.5) for torsade de pointes (TdP), a cardiac arrhythmia, which falls under safety pharmacology.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on predicting torsade de pointes (TdP), a cardiac arrhythmia, which is a cardiovascular safety endpoint.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study compares two different modeling approaches: a single ion channel (hERG) model and a multiple ion channel (MICE) model, thus spanning across different model types.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study uses in vitro assays with ion channels expressed in cell lines (HEK293, CHO) and does not analyze data from whole animals. The focus is on the ion channel behavior itself, not species-specific responses.",
  "endpoint_class": "primary-hard",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study predicts torsade de pointes (TdP), a potentially lethal cardiac arrhythmia, which is a hard clinical outcome."
}
